How we rate peptide products and sellers

Every product and seller is judged on the same five criteria. We publish them so you can check our work.

Peptide Chooser editorial team. Last updated 30 Oct 2026. Every claim links to its source. Prices checked 30 Oct 2026.

1. Evidence

We look for human studies on the specific use you are reading about. Lab and animal results are reported as such and never presented as proof that something works in people.

2. Regulatory status

We state whether a product is FDA-approved for that use, sold as a cosmetic or supplement, compounded by a pharmacy, or labeled for research only. We check the FDA's public warning letter database for every seller we list and link the letter when one exists.

3. Lab testing

We record whether a seller publishes a certificate of analysis (COA), which lab issued it, its date, and whether it is tied to a specific batch. A COA that cannot be matched to a batch counts for less.

4. Real price

Sellers quote prices in different ways. We convert them to a common unit, such as price per milligram or price per 30 days of use, so the numbers can be compared directly.

5. Transparency

We look at who owns the company, where it ships from, its return policy, and whether it labels paid promotions.

What does not affect a rating

Whether a seller pays us a commission. Paid links are labeled and sellers without an affiliate program are rated and listed the same way.

Corrections

If you find an error, email hello@peptidechooser.com with the page and the source. We correct confirmed errors and note the date of the change.
